node.label: Max Weber
node.date_label: 1904: Objectivity in Social Science and Social Policy · 1904: The Protestant Ethic: first part of the 1904–05 publication · 1905: The Protestant Ethic: completion of the 1904–05 publication · 1920: The Protestant Ethic: revised version
node.description: A social theorist and historical political economist whose interpretive sociology combines meaningful action with causal explanation. His methodological writings distinguish value-relevant selection from the evidential work of explaining particular historical configurations.
node.representative_figures_and_works: Objectivity in Social Science and Social Policy (1904); The Protestant Ethic: first part of the 1904–05 publication (1904); The Protestant Ethic: completion of the 1904–05 publication (1905); The Protestant Ethic: revised version (1920).

proposed_edges.relationship: Joins interpretive understanding of meaningful social action with a requirement for causal adequacy.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own methodological excerpt, Definition and §7 read; intelligibility alone does not establish a causal account. Excerpt-based contribution, without adopting historical racial/animal asides.

proposed_edges.relationship: Explains how value-relevant selection identifies a historical problem while causal explanation still requires evidence.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own Objectivity excerpt’s cultural-significance/value-relevance paragraphs read; the theoretical resource concerns selection and explanation, not an assertion that all comparative sociology follows Weber.

weber_method_primary.note: New limited rereading: Definition of Sociology, Methodological Foundations §§1–2 and §7, plus Objectivity paragraphs on cultural significance/value-relevance. Meaningful interpretation must also meet causal evidence; selection is not a licence for arbitrary factual claims. Remaining excerpts not newly reread; prior broader reading and original-German limits preserved.
